name: Plate River
description: Illustrative reusable-plate float seed pitch for food halls.

slides.title: PLATE
items: RIVER
Reusable ceramic float for food halls
Illustrative seed pitch

slides.title: A plate should come back.
items: Food halls burn through single-use ware at lunch and again at dinner. Guests leave trays; nobody owns the return path.
Plate River floats a shared ceramic set through wash, rack and service so the next guest inherits a clean plate, not a new one.

slides.title: Wash is the choke point
items: Plates enter a sealed rack at the tray return. The wash line releases a counted stack to the next service window.
A cracked rim is tagged out of the float. The hall sees available covers before the rush, not after.

slides.title: Service → return → wash → rack
items: Service
Hosts pull a counted stack. The float number rides on the rack card.
Return
Guests leave trays at a single mouth. Mixed ware is sorted before the belt.
Wash
A sealed cycle. Cracked rims exit to the cull bin with a photo tag.
Rack
Clean stacks return to the window with a live cover count.

slides.title: Cost per 100 servings
items: Illustrative hall model • dollars for plate ware across 100 guest servings
Single-use ware stays flat. The float drops after wash labor is absorbed. At 8 washes per plate-life, modeled cost is $4.20 per 100 servings.

slides.title: What a hall pays to float
items: $2,400 / month
Covers 2,000 active plates, wash SLAs, cull replacement and a weekly cover report.
$1,480 direct
Wash labor share $820, cull replacements $360, logistics $300. Contribution $920 before overhead.

slides.title: Begin with one food hall
items: 12 halls
At $2,400 per month, twelve halls produce $345,600 in annual float revenue before cull overages.
Entry test
Enroll a hall only if tray return is single-mouth and the wash line can release a counted stack in under twelve minutes.

slides.title: What halls buy today
items: Single-use
Simple purchasing. Guests leave a pile that never returns to service.
Owned ceramics
Beautiful when staffed. Breakage and wash labor sit on the hall with no shared float.
Plate River
A counted float with a wash SLA and a live cover number before the rush.

slides.title: Two crafts, one float
items: June Park / ceramics ops
June owns cull standards, glaze lots and replacement lead times. A cracked rim never re-enters a guest stack.
Omar Ruiz / hall logistics
Omar owns tray-mouth design and wash-window SLAs. His team publishes the cover count thirty minutes before service.

slides.title: A pilot with three gates
items: Return
90% of trays hit the single mouth for ten consecutive lunch services.
Wash
Counted stacks release in under twelve minutes with fewer than 2% cull tags.
Renew
The hall renews at full price after six weeks of live cover reports.

slides.title: Keep the plates in motion.
items: $3.6M seed
$1.6M for ceramic inventory, $1.1M for wash tooling and logistics, $900k for hall onboarding. Illustrative company and figures.
Target: 12 halls and three renewals inside 15 months.
